content: Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, has the potential to significantly increase the levels of various medications metabolized by the CYP3A4 enzyme. This interaction can lead to an elevated risk of adverse effects, including toxicities. Below are specific considerations for co-administration with lenacapavir: 1. Dexamethasone: Lenacapavir may increase dexamethasone levels, raising the risk of toxicities such as Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Initiate dexamethasone at the lowest dose, monitor closely, and adjust as needed. 2. Dexlansoprazole: Lenacapavir can increase the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Diazepam (oral, buccal, intranasal): Lenacapavir may elevate diazepam levels, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely. 4. Digoxin: Lenacapavir may increase digoxin levels. Monitor therapeutic concentrations carefully. 5. Dihydroergotamine, Ergotamine, Methylergonovine: Co-administration with lenacapavir is not recommended due to the risk of significant increases in drug levels. Use alternative medications. 6. Diltiazem: Lenacapavir may increase diltiazem levels. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 7. Disopyramide: Lenacapavir may elevate disopyramide levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Docetaxel: Lenacapavir may increase docetaxel levels. Monitor closely for toxicity. 9. Doravirine: Lenacapavir may increase doravirine levels. Monitor closely. 10. Doxorubicin (including liposomal formulations): Lenacapavir may elevate doxorubicin levels. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 11. Dronabinol: Lenacapavir may increase dronabinol levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Dronedarone: Lenacapavir may elevate dronedarone levels. Monitor closely. 13. Duvelisib: Lenacapavir may increase duvelisib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Edoxaban: Lenacapavir may increase edoxaban levels. Refer to prescribing information for guidance on co-administration. 15. Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Elacestrant: Lenacapavir may increase elacestrant levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Elagolix: Lenacapavir may increase elagolix levels, while elagolix may decrease lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Lenacapavir may increase levels of these drugs. Monitor closely. 19. Eletriptan: Lenacapavir may elevate eletriptan levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Eliglustat: Lenacapavir may increase eliglustat levels. Monitor closely. 21. Elvitegravir: Lenacapavir may increase elvitegravir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Encorafenib: Lenacapavir may increase encorafenib levels, while encorafenib may decrease lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or adjust encorafenib dose as needed. 23. Enfortumab Vedotin: Lenacapavir may increase enfortumab vedotin levels. Monitor closely. 24. Entrectinib: Lenacapavir may elevate entrectinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases lenacapavir levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Eplerenone: Lenacapavir may increase eplerenone levels. Monitor closely. 27. Ergoloid Mesylates: Lenacapavir may elevate levels of ergoloid mesylates. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ergonovine: Lenacapavir may increase ergonovine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Ergotamine: Lenacapavir significantly increases ergotamine levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Erlotinib: Lenacapavir may elevate erlotinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate): Lenacapavir may increase erythromycin levels. Monitor closely. 32. Escitalopram: Lenacapavir may elevate escitalopram levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Eslicarbazepine Acetate: Eslicarbazepine decreases lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 34. Esomeprazole: Lenacapavir may increase esomeprazole levels. Monitor closely. 35. Estradiol, Estrogens (conjugated synthetic, esterified): Lenacapavir may elevate estrogen levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Estropipate: Lenacapavir may increase estropipate levels. Monitor closely. 37. Eszopiclone: Lenacapavir may elevate eszopiclone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Ethinylestradiol: Lenacapavir may increase ethinylestradiol levels. Monitor closely. 39. Ethosuximide: Lenacapavir may elevate ethosuximide levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Etoposide: Lenacapavir may increase etoposide levels. Monitor closely. 41. Etravirine: Etravirine decreases lenacapavir levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 42. Everolimus: Lenacapavir may elevate everolimus levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Exemestane: Lenacapavir may increase exemestane levels. Monitor closely. 44. Fedratinib: Lenacapavir may elevate fedratinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Felbamate: Lenacapavir may increase felbamate levels. Monitor closely. 46. Felodipine: Lenacapavir may elevate felodipine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Fenofibrate (including micronized formulations): Lenacapavir may increase fenofibrate levels. Monitor closely. 48. Fenofibric Acid: Lenacapavir may elevate fenofibric acid levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Fentanyl (all formulations): Lenacapavir may increase fentanyl levels, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Monitor therapeutic effects and adverse reactions closely. 50. Fexinidazole: Lenacapavir may increase fexinidazole levels. Avoid co-administration or monitor for reduced efficacy. 51. Flibanserin: Lenacapavir significantly increases flibanserin levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 52. Flunisolide (inhaled): Lenacapavir may elevate flunisolide levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Flurazepam: Lenacapavir may increase flurazepam levels. Monitor closely. 54. Flutamide: Lenacapavir may elevate flutamide levels. Use caution and monitor closely. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when lenacapavir is co-administered with other medications metabolized by CYP3A4. In some cases, alternative drugs should be considered to avoid significant interactions.
